summary: Preinstall script executes XOR+AES-GCM obfuscated payload on npm install
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node 3FWCvzduYZg.js`, which auto-runs on `npm install`. That file contains a ~4.4 MB character-code array wrapped in `eval(String.fromCharCode(a[i] ^ 60))`; the decoded ~1.5 MB body imports `crypto`, `fs`, `path`, `os`, and `child_process` and uses `createDecipheriv('aes-128-gcm',...)` with `setAuthTag` to decrypt and execute a further stage on the installer's machine. A second, redundant execution path is embedded in `binding.gyp`: its `conditions` field contains a Python subclass-sandbox-escape expression (`().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()` → `catch_warnings` → `__builtins__` → `__import__('os').system('node 3FWCvzduYZg.js')`) with identifiers hidden as `\U000000xx` unicode escapes, evaluated by node-gyp at configure time. No native source files accompany `binding.gyp`, so its only purpose is to re-trigger the loader. The multi-layer obfuscation (unicode-escape identifiers, XOR-charcode eval, AES-128-GCM inner payload) combined with automatic install-time execution constitutes arbitrary code execution on any host that installs this version.
